dispositions.diagnosisOnFrozenV13: TWO distinct defects, and the blind could only see the first. (a) PUBLISHED LAW: the grammar-capability registry's enforcementBoundary (2) and native 1.2's `Every admitted fact` bullet stated an unconditional every-anchor-path rule while boundary (3) exempted inventory capabilities, so the two bullets contradicted each other and a literal implementer refused a file@enumerated fact for an inventoried .py path whose Coverage the same section had just promised was unconditionally complete. (b) ACTUAL REFERENCE: root is correct that frozen v13 ADMITS the anchored file fact - the model's inventory exemption precedes the grammar check at both call sites - but the probe that establishes that also establishes something worse, which the blind's own implementation hid from it: BOTH the anchored and the unanchored spelling of one file@enumerated claim close a Run, with DIFFERENT fact2 identities (5cce76d9... and d7bb2235... over tool/main.py), on every path including supported ones, and the same holds for vcs-change. Three further live gaps fell out of the same probe: an unanchored `declares`/`references`/`types` fact closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe (the `an unanchored code fact is not vacuously supported` rule was enforced only inside the syntax-universe guard); a package@manifest-declared fact claiming package.json closed a Run while anchored into an unrelated a.ts (anchorPathField existed only on the `file` row); and a file@enumerated Coverage claimed `complete` over the inventoried subject a.ts with zero facts, so `exists file where path=a.ts` was authoritatively FALSE over a complete result.
dispositions.whyTheBlindsProposedRemedyIsNotSufficien: The blind offered `state the anchor cardinality per relation, OR exempt the three inventory capabilities from boundary (2)`. Neither alone closes it. The exemption alone leaves both spellings admissible and the identity non-canonical - which is the defect the actual reference exhibits and the blind's own implementation concealed. The cardinality alone leaves the published boundary (2) contradicting boundary (3), so a conformant independent implementation still refuses inventory facts the contract promises. Both are needed, and neither addresses the complete-empty-inventory hole at all.
selectedLaw: Relation registry gains a CLOSED per-relation `anchorLaw` in three classes, with no default row: `source-text` (the nine code relations) minimum 1; `body-identity` (clones) exactly 1; `inventory` (file, package, vcs-change) exactly 0. Enforced once, in identity-model relation_payload_rules, before the snapshot joins and before the syntax capability guard, at the producer boundary and again at retained Run closure.

Zero for the inventory class because such a fact is not read from a source span: its whole semantic input is its payload, which the relation's own snapshotJoins already bind (path in the inventory; for `file` also the content digest, the byte length and CUSTODY of the retained bytes). An anchor restates part of an already-joined claim on an axis nothing derives. Zero is also the ONLY cardinality every inventoried path can satisfy - unsupported suffix, extensionless, data-document, and decisively a vcs-change on a `deleted` path that the registry itself places outside the snapshot and that can bear no anchor at all. Cardinality 1 would make that case unrepresentable and would newly require every package manifest's bytes to be retained.

The `source-text` class deliberately has NO upper bound and NO canonical extent, and the registry says so: which spans a producer cites is a real statement about what it read, so differing citations are DIFFERENT semantic descriptors that legitimately mint different identities. No cross-provider anchor identity is promised for code facts, per root's explicit caution.

Published boundary (2) now carries the inventory exemption alongside boundary (3), with the reason stated: the exemption belongs to the RELATION, not the boundary, because an inventory fact is not read by a grammar at all. The two laws are independent and agree - an inventory fact also names no anchor path for boundary (2) to test - and the exemption is from GRAMMAR OWNERSHIP only: snapshot joins, own-scope attribution and the anchor law all still bind, and no code fact becomes admissible because another anchor in the Run is supported.

New registry `coverageTotality` row on `file` only: a `complete` file@enumerated Coverage must carry an admitted fact for every subject the snapshot inventory contains (COVERAGE_INVENTORY_TOTALITY_OMITS_PATH), derived at Run closure from the retained view's own facts and the retained inventory. A subject the snapshot does NOT contain is owed nothing, and an `unknown` result with its disclosed deficiency is owed nothing. package and vcs-change are NOT total and get no row: most paths declare no package and most were not changed.
bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality becomes a declared MIRROR of the clones anchorLaw; the join checks the two AGREE (RELATION_ANCHOR_LAW_DRIFT) instead of refusing one fault twice under two names.
dispositions.tradeoffs: The `file` row's anchorPathField becomes unreachable under cardinality 0. Two existing controls changed their expected refusal REASON (not their outcome) and are updated with the reason recorded.
dispositions.residual: Whether a real host's enumerator produces exactly one inventory fact per inventoried path remains a trusted observation; the totality law binds the CLAIM, not the observation.

dispositions.diagnosisOnFrozenV13: Confirmed exactly: section 10 labels its column `Cause (nativeCause)` and three rows name values the closed NativeCause cannot express - computed-member-access, exports-open and compiler-inferred each fail schema validation there. But the schema refusal was only half of it. Nothing COMPARED the pair to anything, so on frozen v13 a resolution-incomplete entry carrying the unrelated but schema-valid lockfile-missing ADMITTED, as did the same entry relabelled capability-missing, a resolution-incomplete over a COMPLETE resolution, an external-consumers-unknown over exportsClosed=closed, a derivation-policy-unmet over an empty derivationKinds, an input-closure-incomplete with a null cause, a budget-exhausted with no budget stage terminal, and a cause with no deficiency at all.
dispositions.whyTheBlindsProposedRemedyIsNotSufficien: The blind offered `three to twenty new NativeCause members, or one sentence saying these causes travel in resolutionCompleteness and closedWorld`. New members are wrong on the merits: resolution-incomplete has a genuinely SET-VALUED cause (up to all sixteen UnresolvedEdgeKindV1 classes at once), so a scalar loses information or forces an arbitrary pick - the multi-cause defect itself. And one sentence is insufficient: it leaves every substitution above admissible, which is precisely the `a vocabulary nothing derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional` argument the v13 ownership correction already made.
selectedLaw: A CLOSED x-opensip-deficiency-cause-registry over every DeficiencyV2 member, with no default row, naming per deficiency WHICH retained field carries its cause and WHAT that field must say. NO enum changes anywhere: not NativeCause, not DeficiencyV2, not UnresolvedEdgeKindV1, not the public DomainDetailCode registry, no D9 class, code or exit. Every carrier already existed and is already closed.

The three named rows get their real carriers: resolution-incomplete -> resolutionCompleteness (state in {incomplete, partial, not-attempted}, with unresolvedEdgeClasses carrying ALL applicable classes at once and already forced by RC-2 to equal the view's admitted unresolved-edge facts); external-consumers-unknown -> closedWorld.exportsClosed in {open, unknown}; derivation-policy-unmet -> derivationKinds contains compiler-inferred. Their nativeCause is null BY DESIGN and that null is no longer an escape, because admission refuses unless the named field actually carries the cause.

The remaining rows are named too: language-tier-unsupported requires exactly capability-missing; input-closure-incomplete requires one of the twelve; budget-exhausted requires stageTerminal = budget-exhausted; provider-unavailable is self-describing with two optional causes; confidence-floor-unmet and required-relation-missing are requirement-relative and have NO entry carrier, which is stated as a limit rather than given an invented predicate. A null deficiency requires a null cause.

Multi-cause and precedence: an entry carries ONE deficiency and EVERY carrier simultaneously, and the carriers are structurally independent, so the scalar loses nothing. Which member is declared when several apply is the published section 10 precedence, applied by the sufficiency evaluation against a REQUIREMENT.
Enforced in admit_coverage_result_v3 - the producer boundary - and therefore again at close_run, which re-runs that exact admission over the RETAINED payload.
dispositions.whatWasDeliberatelyNotDone: No entry-level OBLIGATION is derived: the enforced direction is only that a DECLARED deficiency must be SUPPORTED by the entry's own committed evidence. Forcing a deficiency from exhibited entry evidence would refuse lawful Runs, because RC-3 makes `coverage: complete` with `state: incomplete` and NO deficiency a valid honest entry (the v13 corpus fixture coverageIncompletePayload is exactly that), and because external-consumer state and the confidence floor are requirement-relative. The registry states that limit instead of papering over it, and a control holds the RC-3 entry lawful.

dispositions.diagnosisOnFrozenV13: Confirmed, and worse than a naming gap. capabilityId is `$ref: Text` and enters PlanId through analysisSpecDigest with no named vocabulary, and THREE spellings were in live use in one release: the default-selection corpus emitted relation@rung (clones@normalized-body-hash), the foundation reference fixture emitted a bare relation name (references), and the matrix publishes inventory/syntax/clones-fact/... selectedLaw: The vocabulary authority is published with its exact selector: native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json#/capabilities[].id, closed at eleven, with the law at #/capabilityIdLaw and the schema annotated to point at it. A capability id and a relation@rung are declared DIFFERENT CONCEPTS and are not equated: a capability is a requestable unit of work covering several relations (inventory covers three) or none (clones-near, clones-cross-tsjs are candidate-only); a relation@rung is a fact/Coverage coordinate. The matrix's own capabilities[].relations is the published bridge in both directions.
